about: Seed notes for the Apricity wine study tool, taken from the prototype wine map (Nov 2026). Notes are style estimates from the producer, grape and region, not tasting notes. Prices and vintages are a snapshot; the live wine sheet wins.

wines.note: The Cava grapes with no added sugar: apple, fennel, almond, very dry. The best-value bottle of fizz.
Greek natural sparkling. Expect Malagousia's floral, peachy aroma with Assyrtiko's citrus and salt.
Natural, very low or no added sugar: ripe apple and pear, creamy, softer acidity than the English wines.
Traditional method, the Champagne recipe grown in England: green apple, lemon, brioche, high acidity. The reference fizz.
Chalk-grown, partly barrel-fermented, low dosage: red apple, stone fruit, pastry. Broader than Roebuck.
Aged Riesling fizz: lime, honey, a petrol note, toast.
A long-aged blanc de noirs: richer, with red fruit, toast and nuttiness.
A young grower from southern Champagne. Pinot Blanc adds soft, pear-like fruit. Ripe, fruity, dry. The entry Champagne.
Biodynamic rosé Champagne from the Marne Valley: red berries, chalk, fine bubbles, dry.
Blanc de blancs from top chalk villages: precise, lemony, chalky, fine. The lean, pure end of the Champagnes.
Blanc de blancs from Avize, raised in oak: broader and more wine-like than Monts Fournois.
Organic since 1971, barrel-fermented, no added sugar. Rich, vinous and intense, like a white wine with bubbles.
Made by Vincent Laval, who runs Georges Laval, from his uncle's vines. Ask your supplier what sets it apart.
Son of Champagne's most famous grower. Pinot Noir from the Aube: powerful, nutty, oxidative in style. The richest sparkling wine here.
The house collaboration, made from wine that would otherwise go unused. Riesling-led: lime, green apple, light body. Confirm how dry it is.
Biodynamic Grüner Veltliner: green apple, white pepper, herbs, light. A peppery alternative to Sauvignon.
Organic English white: elderflower, hedgerow, grapefruit, dry and light. England's answer to Sauvignon.
Natural Sauvignon from the Puzelat family: riper and softer than Sancerre, less grassy, more orchard fruit.
Biodynamic Muscadet: lemon, sea salt, lean and neutral, made for oysters.
Loire Chenin: apple, quince, a honeyed edge, bright acidity. The entry Chenin.
Soft, floral, pear and apple, gentle acidity. Easy and friendly.
Vines grown in pits of black volcanic ash on Lanzarote. Floral, citrus, salty, smoky.
Old-vine Sylvaner, natural: herbal, green apple, lightly textured.
A small natural farm in Kent. Expect Bacchus aroma with Chardonnay body.
Chablis growers working with Alsace fruit. Very aromatic (rose, lychee, grape) but dry. The most perfumed dry white.
Unoaked northern Burgundy: orchard fruit, citrus, oyster shell. Your anchor for a lean, mineral white.
Ribolla gives lemon, green apple and high acidity. Check whether this one has skin contact.
Textbook Sancerre: gooseberry, citrus, a flinty edge. The most familiar white on the list.
Alpine and light, about 11%: white flowers, pear, hay, mouthwatering.
Topped-up Jura Savagnin, so fresh, not sherry-like: lemon, green apple, a nutty hint, piercing acidity.
Volcanic soils near the Hungarian border: quince, pear, smoke, firm acidity.
Biodynamic, near the Mediterranean: stone fruit, herbs, salt. Fresh for a southern white.
Savoie Altesse: quince, honey and almond with firm acidity. Richer than Monfarina.
Old vines on Tenerife's volcanic soil, aged in large old casks. Smoky, salty, lemony, struck-match.
Atlantic and intense: lime, sea spray, very high acidity.
Natural Aligoté, Burgundy's other white grape: sharper, lemony, lighter than Chardonnay.
Biodynamic, long barrel ageing, no added sulfur. Not typical Sauvignon: nutty, herbal, stony and textured.
Biodynamic pioneers on steep slate, no added sulfur. Dry, lime and apple, stony, a little wild.
Southern Burgundy, so riper and rounder: yellow apple, peach.
Natural Jura Chardonnay: lemon, a nutty and savoury edge, high acidity. Wilder than any Burgundy here.
A small, precise, low-sulfur Burgundy house. Their entry Chardonnay: purity and tension.
Serious Aligoté: citrus, chalk, real length.
A famous low-intervention Burgundy name. Village-level white: ripe fruit, some oak, mineral finish.
An organic Sicilian co-operative. Lemon, almond, herbs, easy. The cheapest white.

wines.grapes: Clairette, Grenache Gris, Grenache Blanc & Bourboulenc
wines.note: Biodynamic Languedoc blend: peach, fennel, soft and round, gentle acidity. Your anchor for a rounder white.
A rare grape from one small Loire appellation: high acidity, quince, honey, waxy. Like a sharper Chenin.
Barrel-fermented on Kent chalk: apple, citrus, toast. The oaked contrast to the Vézelay.
Natural Sicilian white with more character than the Valdibella.
Biodynamic Rhône Marsanne: apricot, honeysuckle, almond; broad and low in acid.
White Rioja from an organic family estate: apple, fennel, waxy texture.
Peach, lemon, saline, generous. The softer, rounder Albariño.
Natural Slovak Chardonnay, no added sulfur. Expect savoury, slightly nutty and unconventional.
Biodynamic Abruzzo Pecorino: citrus, mountain herbs, salty, with grip.
Biodynamic pioneer, no sulfur. Soft, low acid, yellow apple, nutty, a cidery edge.
Old-vine field blend from granite mountains in the Dão: citrus, stone, textured but taut.
Essex fruit made in London. Barrel-fermented, Burgundy-style, ripe and creamy.
Ligurian Pigato, the local Vermentino: herbs, peach, sea salt, a little skin texture.
Oak and amphora aged Sauvignon: smoky, textured, ripe. The bridge between Sancerre and Muster Graf.
A natural-wine icon from Faugères. Rich, nutty, apricot, deliberately oxidative.
Matassa wines are light, low in alcohol, salty and wild.
Biodynamic New Zealand Chardonnay on limestone: concentrated citrus, oak, bright fruit.
The Jura's star grower: long barrel ageing, intense, struck-match, mineral. Check the cuvée name.
Barrel-aged Saumur Chenin: quince, chalk, tension, length. The grown-up Vin de Frantz.
Single-vineyard Chardonnay: precise, pure, built to age.
Single-vineyard Chardonnay from the hills above Beaune: precise, pure, built to age.
A legendary traditional estate; grapes trodden by foot, aged in concrete. Dense, savoury, long-lived.
A tiny cult Jura estate; bottles are very hard to find. The rarest white on the list.
Pale, dry Provence rosé: strawberry and citrus. What most guests picture as rosé.
Clarete ferments white and red grapes together: deeper colour, savoury, herbal. More like a light red.
Biodynamic Sicilian rosé: cherry, blood orange, fuller.
English Pinot rosé: redcurrant, crisp, high acid. Sharper and leaner than Provence.
Natural, small production. Sits between rosé and light red.
Red grapes listed under orange, so ask how it is made and what colour it pours.
Aromatic Muscat with skin contact: orange peel, flowers, light tannin.
From a founding family of modern orange wine; their young, lighter bottling. Apricot, tea, herbs. The by-the-glass introduction.
Light, floral, grapey, low alcohol, gentle grip. The friendliest orange wine.
La Stoppa makes one of Italy's benchmark orange wines: apricot, dried flowers, firm tannin. Check the cuvée.
Skin-fermented Styrian Sauvignon with long ageing: herbal, stony, savoury.
Long skin contact from a revered natural farm: amber, structured, tannic, complex. The most serious orange.
Organic co-operative Nero d'Avola: plum, cherry, soft, uncomplicated. The cheapest red.
A Czech crossing of Blaufränkisch and St Laurent: dark berries, spice, bright acidity, some age. A bargain.
Light, rustic Tuscan Sangiovese: cherry, pomegranate, herbs. The first step on the Sangiovese ladder.
Low alcohol, peppery, crunchy red fruit; serve cool. The lightest red.
The reference Blaufränkisch: sour cherry, black pepper, iron, fresh.
Natural Carignan: dark fruit, herbs, lively acidity.
Galician Mencía: floral, red-fruited, fresh, a little herbal. The Spanish answer to Beaujolais.
Alpine Italy. Pale, light, strawberry and almond, with a little dark fruit from the Lagrein. Your anchor light red.
From the best-known Czech natural winemaker. Expect juicy, bright, playful.
Natural Ardèche red, juicy and dark-fruited.
Xinomavro behaves like Nebbiolo: pale, tomato leaf, olive, firm tannin and acidity.
Alpine Swiss Pinot: light, red cherry, herbal. The start of the Pinot ladder.
Serious Beaujolais from granite: raspberry, violet, mineral, silky. The bridge to the Pinot Noirs.
Alsace Pinot with no sulfur: light, crunchy, a little wild.
English natural red: very light, tart red berries.
Pale, low in alcohol and made like an infusion, even though it is Syrah.
Mountain Pinot from Savoie: fresh, red-fruited, fine.
From vines in Volnay and Pommard: silky, light, pure red fruit. The cleanest, most classic Burgundy entry.
A pioneering natural farm. Peppery, earthy, wild, light-bodied. The wildest light red.
Pale, low-alcohol Cinsault made like an infusion.
A young natural grower in the hills above Beaune: bright, juicy, energetic.
Pinot Noir and Gamay from the Jura: juicy, crunchy, very drinkable.
Whole-bunch, low sulfur: perfumed, precise, fine tannins.
Single-vineyard Burgundy: perfumed, precise, fine tannins.
A cult natural grower above Nuits-Saint-Georges. Wild, intense, divisive.
Whole-bunch village Burgundy: dark cherry, spice, more structure. The classic top of the Pinot ladder.
A legendary natural estate in Nuits-Saint-Georges. Perfumed, whole-bunch, no added sulfur.
Unoaked Barbera: sour cherry, high acidity, very little tannin. Juicier than its section suggests.
Biodynamic Ardèche red: juicy plum, licorice, soft tannin, fresher than most Rhône reds. Your anchor for ripe and generous.
A natural family farm in Slovakia; a blend across grapes and years.
Dunaj is a dark Slovak grape: plum, black cherry, spice, some age.
Young-vine Nebbiolo, no oak: pale colour, rose and cherry, then a firm grip of tannin. Little brother of his Barolo.
Biodynamic Moravian Frankovka on rocky soils: dark cherry, pepper, mineral, structured.
No added sulfur, schist soils. Meaty, herbal (thyme, bay), smoky. Wilder and more savoury than Bout d'Zan.
Loire Cabernet Franc: raspberry, pencil shavings, a leafy green note, fresh.
Biodynamic benchmark from the Dolomites: dark berries, violet, fresh, moderate tannin.

wines.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Malbec, Cabernet Franc
wines.note: Biodynamic Bordeaux: cassis, plum, cedar, firm tannin. The most classic red on the list; your anchor for firm and structured.
Over ten years old: softened tannin, dried cherry, leather, spice. Shows what age does to Blaufränkisch.
Volcanic-soil Blaufränkisch from Slovakia: spicy, sour cherry, fine tannin.
From the slopes of Vesuvius: red fruit, smoke, ash, savoury. The volcanic red.
Natural southern Rhône with a few years of age: dark fruit, garrigue herbs, warmth. Bout d'Zan with more power.
Barrel-aged Savoie Mondeuse: blackberry, black pepper, violet, firm tannin.
Fine, perfumed Cabernet Franc with silky tannin and real depth.
Natural-wine pioneers. Pure Syrah: black olive, pepper, violet, fresh rather than heavy. The Syrah reference.
Sour cherry, orange, herbs, leather; firm but ripe. The middle of the Sangiovese ladder.
Old-vine Garnacha at altitude in Rioja: tight, mineral, dark cherry, fine tannin, not oaky. Listed under Rhône by mistake.
New Zealand Pinot, riper and darker than Burgundy: black cherry, spice, more body.
From a revered natural farm in the Maremma: deep, earthy, structured, long-lived. Top of the Sangiovese ladder.
The Rhône's sturdiest Syrah: dark, smoky, meaty, firm tannin.
An aromatic Muscat-family grape: orange blossom, grape, light. Check how sweet it is.
Sweet Tokaj: apricot, honey, bright acidity.
A fortified red, like a young Port: blackberry, chocolate, sweet. The one for chocolate puddings.
Made from dried grapes: apricot jam, honey, orange peel, rich.
Late-harvest, biodynamic Jurançon: pineapple, honey, razor acidity. The finest sweet wine.
Twenty-year-old sweet Riesling: honey, lime marmalade, petrol, light in alcohol.
A pink pét-nat: low alcohol, soft bubbles, strawberry and violet, a touch of sweetness.
Sicilian Grillo: citrus, herbs and a salty finish with some weight.
